subject: At what distance do I miss a given proportion?

messages.author: fa112d5a5313e536
messages.subject: At what distance do I miss a given proportion?
parts:
Dear All,

 I would like to know what proportion of animals I miss at a given distance from the line. I understand that the ESW is calculated by multiplying the Detection Probability by Truncation distance, and as a result I get the distance at which observation missed is before the ESW is equal to observations observed beyond the ESW. However, if I want to know for example at what distance 25% of my objects are missed, how do I calculate that? Would this be equivalent to a probability density function (PDF), which is different to the plot.ds() probability detection function? Is there a way I could plot this?

Many thanks for any pointers and suggestions.

 Kind regards,

 Don

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] At what distance do I miss a given proportion?
parts:
Don

I believe the answer is simpler than you are trying to make it.  Section 1.5 of Buckland et al. (2015) defines the *detection function g(x)* as "the probability of detecting an animal that is at distance x from the transect (0 < x < w)".  Using plot.ds() will show you the fitted detection function and you can interpret the values from that curve as you describe.  For a value x satisfying g(x)=0.75, that x corresponds to the distance at which 25% of the objects located at that distance are missed.

The computation of ESW uses what we denote as P_a multiplied by w.  The quantity P_a is the probability that an object is detected, given it is *anywhere* up to distance w from the transect.

parts:
Thanks Eric,

I do hope its simpler than I am making it! However, excuse my slow comprehension on this. Yes, I understand that g(x)=0.75 is equal to 25% of animals missed at that given distance. But, does that equate to the 25% of all animals missed at a distance at g(x) out ward to the truncation distance? For example, in my case, I have a dung survey with a truncation distance at 2 meters.  g(x) at 0.75 is at 1.85 meters. Does that mean I am missing 25% of all observations between 0<g<2 at a distance beyond 1.85 meters? Or, if I have 100 dung piles in a strip transect of 2 meters, I would be missing 25% on the last 15 cm?

Again, thanks so much for your time in explaing this to me. Much appreciated!

Don

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] At what distance do I miss a given proportion?
parts:
Don, that is not the question you asked.  You asked: ‘at what distance 25% of my objects are missed’.  That distance is the distance at which g(x)=0.75, as Eric stated.  The question you’re now asking is ‘Suppose I have 100 dung piles in the strip.  What is the distance beyond which I fail to detect 25 dung piles?’  This seems a rather odd quantity to want to estimate – I can’t see what use it could be put to.  It can be estimated.  If the truncation distance is w, it is the distance d such that the area above g(x) for d<x<w is 25% of w.

 

Steve Buckland
